heard: a cosmic giant crowned the biggest star in the universe suddenly shrank. Back in 1860, astronomers at the Bonn Observatory cataloged a faint star in the constellation Scutum. Originally designated as BD-12 degrees 5055, its flickering brightness revealed a pulsating variable star. In 2012, very large telescope interferometry in Chile calculated a staggering radius of 1,708 solar radii. This massive size crowned UiSQT the largest known star, with a volume swallowing Jupiter's orbit. However, newer Gaia space telescope data revised its distance closer to Earth. The updated measurements shrank its official radius down to approximately 909 solar radii. A cosmic giant crowned the biggest star in the universe suddenly shrank.
